# Multi-Tenant Document Store API Design

## Resources & Endpoints

```
Documents (primary resource)
  POST   /v1/documents                 Create doc
  GET    /v1/documents                 List docs (paginated)
  GET    /v1/documents/{id}            Get doc
  PUT    /v1/documents/{id}            Update doc
  DELETE /v1/documents/{id}            Delete doc
  GET    /v1/documents/{id}/versions   List versions
  GET    /v1/documents/{id}/versions/{version_id}  Get specific version

Document Collections (organize docs)
  POST   /v1/collections               Create collection
  GET    /v1/collections               List collections
  PUT    /v1/collections/{id}          Update collection
  DELETE /v1/collections/{id}          Delete collection

Sharing & Access Control
  POST   /v1/documents/{id}/share      Grant access to user/team
  DELETE /v1/documents/{id}/share/{user_id}  Revoke access
  GET    /v1/documents/{id}/access     List who has access
```

**Why:** Separate collections from docs keeps structure simple. Sharing as explicit resource models permission model clearly.

---

## Auth Model

**Header-based JWT with tenant context:**
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

JWT payload:
{
  "sub": "user_123",
  "tenant_id": "org_456",
  "email": "user@company.com",
  "roles": ["editor", "viewer"],
  "iat": 1726000000,
  "exp": 1726086400
}
```

**Tenant isolation strategy:**
- Tenant ID extracted from JWT token, not from URL
- Every query scoped to `tenant_id` from token at DB layer
- No `?tenant_id=` params (prevents elevation bugs)
- Rate limits per tenant, not per IP

**Why:** JWT in token avoids URL-based injection bugs. Tenant in token → can't switch tenants mid-request. Server-enforced scope prevents query/mutation escapes.

**Authorization:** Row-level via `documents.owner_id`, `shared_access` table:
```sql
-- Fetch only docs this user owns or can access
SELECT * FROM documents 
WHERE tenant_id = :tenant_id 
AND (owner_id = :user_id OR id IN (
  SELECT document_id FROM shared_access 
  WHERE user_id = :user_id AND revoked = false
))
```

---

## Pagination

**Cursor-based (not offset) for stability:**

```
GET /v1/documents?limit=25&cursor=abc123xyz

Response:
{
  "data": [ ... 25 docs ... ],
  "pagination": {
    "next_cursor": "def456uvw",
    "has_more": true,
    "count": 25
  }
}
```

**Why:** Cursor survives insertions/deletions mid-pagination. Offset skips/duplicates rows when list changes. Cursor uses indexed `created_at + id` → O(1) lookup. Better UX for real-time lists.

**Limit defaults to 25, max 100.** Prevents runaway queries.

---

## API Versioning

**URL-based (path prefix), not headers:**
```
/v1/documents   ← current stable
/v2/documents   ← next breaking change when ready
```

**Why:** Simpler ops (one version live per URL path). Clients explicit about version consumed. Easy to monitor adoption, deprecate old versions. Header versioning hides version coupling.

**Deprecation:** 
- v1 supported for 12 months after v2 launch
- `Deprecation: true` header in v1 responses after day 1
- `Sunset: 2027-10-12T00:00:00Z` tells clients when v1 dies

---

## Error Format

**Consistent JSON error envelope:**

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "Document 'doc_789' not found or access denied.",
    "status": 404,
    "timestamp": "2026-10-12T14:23:45Z",
    "request_id": "req_abc123xyz",
    "details": {
      "document_id": "doc_789",
      "tenant_id": "org_456"
    }
  }
}
```

**Error codes (machine-readable):**
- `UNAUTHORIZED` (401) — missing/invalid token
- `FORBIDDEN` (403) — token valid, no access to resource
- `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND` (404) — doc doesn't exist or not accessible
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` (400) — bad input (include field errors)
- `CONFLICT` (409) — concurrent edit or duplicate
- `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (429) — tenant hit doc/storage limit
- `INTERNAL_ERROR` (500) — unhandled server error

**Why:** `request_id` lets support trace logs. `code` stays stable even if message changes. `details` context-specific. Separate `UNAUTHORIZED` from `FORBIDDEN` (client knows if auth broke vs permission).

---

## Versioning Strategy (Document History)

**Immutable versions, explicit updates:**
```
PUT /v1/documents/{id}

Body:
{
  "title": "Updated Title",
  "content": "New content here",
  "change_note": "Fixed typo in abstract"
}

Response:
{
  "id": "doc_789",
  "version": 3,
  "title": "Updated Title",
  "content": "New content here",
  "change_note": "Fixed typo in abstract",
  "created_at": "2026-10-01T10:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-12T14:23:45Z",
  "updated_by": "user_123"
}
```

**Version history stored separately:**
```
GET /v1/documents/{id}/versions

[
  { "version": 3, "created_at": "2026-10-12...", "created_by": "user_123", "change_note": "..." },
  { "version": 2, "created_at": "2026-10-10...", "created_by": "user_456", "change_note": "..." },
  { "version": 1, "created_at": "2026-10-01...", "created_by": "user_123", "change_note": "..." }
]

GET /v1/documents/{id}/versions/2  ← fetch full doc at v2
```

**Why:** Immutable history prevents accidental changes. `change_note` required (audit trail). Version number in response clarifies which edit client has. Separate endpoint for versions keeps list endpoint fast.

---

## Example Request/Response

**Create document:**
```bash
POST /v1/documents
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "title": "Q3 Financial Report",
  "content": "Revenue up 15% YoY...",
  "collection_id": "coll_001",
  "tags": ["finance", "q3"]
}
```

**Response (201 Created):**
```json
{
  "id": "doc_789",
  "version": 1,
  "title": "Q3 Financial Report",
  "content": "Revenue up 15% YoY...",
  "collection_id": "coll_001",
  "tags": ["finance", "q3"],
  "owner_id": "user_123",
  "created_at": "2026-10-12T14:23:45Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-12T14:23:45Z",
  "access_level": "private"
}
```

---

## Key Decisions Summary

| Decision | Why |
|----------|-----|
| **JWT in auth header** | Tenant context server-enforced, no URL elevation bugs |
| **Cursor pagination** | Survives concurrent inserts/deletes, stable for real-time lists |
| **URL versioning** | Explicit, ops-simple, easy to deprecate |
| **Separate `FORBIDDEN` vs `UNAUTHORIZED`** | Clients know if auth failed or permission denied |
| **Immutable versions with change_note** | Audit trail, undo-able, no data loss |
| **Collections as resource** | Cleaner org than nested endpoints |
| **Row-level access in DB** | Prevents query-layer escapes, single source of truth |

Main tradeoff: URL versioning means multiple code paths live simultaneously (maintenance cost) vs clearer client contracts. Worth it for multi-tenant SaaS.
